Article Title: Hours into probe, police yet to find motive behind Sukhbir Badal's attack
Article Text:
Hours of interrogation, motive still unclear

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked near a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded on Thursday, leaving him with injuries to his hand. One of his security personnel also sustained injuries.Badal, who has a ‘Z+’ security cover, was injured after Jaspal Singh, a man believed to be around 60-62 years old, attacked him with a ‘kirpan’ (ceremonial dagger) inside a gurdwara.Despite hours of questioning by multiple agencies, police were yet to establish a clear motive for the attack.Police said Jaspal Singh, who holds degrees in commerce and law and is a resident of Pune, was taken to the Nanded police headquarters for questioning.“Despite long hours of interrogation, the police are yet to find a concrete reason for the attack. So far, we have not found any criminal links or any such connections involving the accused in this case,” an official was quoted as saying by news agency PTI.“We are interrogating the accused, and it will go on for a long time. The former Punjab deputy CM Sukhbir Singh Badal is fine and will be discharged soon,” he added.The Anti-Terrorism Squad (ATS) and Intelligence Bureau (IB) have joined the local police in the investigation, an official told PTI.Police have registered a case against Singh at Mudkhed police station in Nanded under Sections 109(1) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), pertaining to attempt to murder; 118(1), relating to voluntarily causing hurt with dangerous weapons or means; and 121(2), concerning voluntarily causing grievous hurt to a public servant to deter them from performing their duty.Singh had been working as a sewadar, or volunteer, at Gurdwara Mata Sahib Devan Ji Mugat for the past two years and was living alone in Nanded, police said.Police officer Santosh Kendre, who is part of Badal’s Special Protection Unit, was injured while shielding him during the attack. Badal was walking down a flight of stairs when Singh allegedly attacked him.
Article Summary: Sikhomani Akali Dal (SAD) president Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked near a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded on Thursday. Badal, who has a ‘Z+’ security cover, was injured after Jaspal Singh, a man believed to be around 60-62 years old, attacked him. One of his security personnel also sustained injuries.

Article Title: Harsimrat Kaur Badal 'deeply touched' by PM Modi's 'kind gesture' after attack on Sukhbir Badal
Article Text:
Sukhbir Badal was attacked at a gurudwara in Maharashtra's Nanded

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal on Friday said she was “deeply touched” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s “kind gesture” of reaching out to enquire about the health of her husband and party chief, Sukhbir Singh Badal , who was attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded a day earlier.This marked the Badal family's first reaction to the attack on the former Punjab deputy chief minister."Truly grateful, Hon’ble Prime Minister Shri @narendramodi ji, for your personal call to inquire about Sardar Sukhbir Singh Badal ji’s health and for your good wishes for his speedy recovery following the dastardly attack on him inside a Gurudwara Sahib in Nanded, Maharashtra," Harsimrat Badal, SAD's only Lok Sabha MP, wrote on X.She also thanked the prime minister for taking immediate cognisance of the incident and directing central investigating agencies to coordinate with the state police in the probe."Your concern, support and wishes during this difficult time mean a lot to all of us in the family, our party and to the people of Punjab. I am deeply touched by your kind gesture. I am also grateful to you for taking immediate cognisance of the incident and directing central investigating agencies to coordinate with Maharashtra Police in the probe," the Bathinda MP added.On Thursday, Sukhbir Singh Badal was injured after being attacked by a kirpan-wielding assailant while leaving the Mata Sahib Devaji Gurdwara at Mudkhed in Maharashtra’s Nanded district. The assailant was arrested at the spot.Maharashtra chief minister Devendra Fadnavis ordered an inquiry into the attack and spoke to Sukhbir Singh Badal over the phone. The SAD president is learnt to have told Fadnavis that he was stable, ANI reported.Earlier, Badal was also targeted in an attempted shooting at the Golden Temple in Amritsar in December 2024 while he was performing “seva”. The attacker allegedly tried to fire at him but was overpowered before he could cause any harm.The 2024 attack took place while Badal was carrying out “seva” after the Akal Takht, the highest temporal authority in Sikhism, declared him a “tankhaiya,” or guilty of religious misconduct, over decisions taken by the SAD-led Punjab government between 2007 and 2017.The SAD and BJP, which currently lead the governments at the Centre and in Maharashtra, are former allies. In 2020, the SAD ended its alliance with the BJP in protest against the Centre’s contentious farm laws, which were later withdrawn.Sukhbir Singh Badal met Prime Minister Narendra Modi last week, triggering speculation that the former allies could reunite ahead of the Punjab assembly elections early next year.
Article Summary: Harsimrat Kaur Badal said she was “deeply touched” by Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s “kind gesture” of reaching out to enquire about the health of her husband and party chief. Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra’s Nanded a day earlier.

Article Title: Bangladesh PM likely to visit India as Dhaka presses for Sheikh Hasina's extradition
Article Text:
Tarique Rahman likely to visit India

Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s proposed visit to India has not yet been finalised, with the timing dependent on his “schedule” and the “progress” of ongoing bilateral discussions."The government is positive about visits to all countries. But it will depend on the PM's schedule and on how far discussions between the two countries progress," state minister for foreign affairs Shama Obaed Islam said."The government is busy, and so is the prime minister. If everything fits together, of course there will be a visit to India, a visit to Japan; all the visits will happen," she said, referring to ongoing domestic programmes and upcoming constitutional activities.In April, Bangladesh foreign minister Khalilur Rahman visited India as part of efforts to mend strained bilateral ties following more than 18 months of heightened diplomatic tensions.Bangladesh has also sought the extradition of former prime minister Sheikh Hasina.External affairs ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said on Tuesday that India has extended two separate invitations to Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman — one for a bilateral visit and another to attend the outreach session of the Brics Summit in New Delhi in September."Brics is still a long way off. A lot can happen in a month,” Shama said.Asked whether Rahman’s visit to India could help ease tensions, Shama said direct communication between the leaders of the two governments could provide an opportunity to discuss and resolve outstanding issues."Whenever the heads of two countries talk, there is a chance of resolving many problems. That opportunity is there; it remains," she said.Relations between India and Bangladesh deteriorated sharply after the interim government led by Muhammad Yunus came to power following the fall of Sheikh Hasina’s government in August 2024.Efforts to stabilise ties gained momentum after Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla, accompanied by foreign secretary Vikram Misri, represented India at Tarique Rahman’s swearing-in ceremony in Dhaka on February 17.Rahman assumed office as prime minister after his party secured a landslide victory in the parliamentary elections.Bangladesh’s current government, led by Rahman’s Bangladesh Nationalist Party, has maintained that Sheikh Hasina must surrender and face the law if she returns to the country.Hasina recently addressed an audio-only virtual press conference from New Delhi, her first public media interaction since fleeing to India on August 5, 2024, amid mass protests.During the virtual press conference, Hasina said she was determined to return to Bangladesh in December to put the country on the "right track" by restoring democracy, despite facing the possibility of imprisonment or a death sentence.India distanced itself from Hasina’s media interaction, clarifying that it had neither played a role in organising the event nor endorsed her remarks concerning the Bangladesh government.
Article Summary: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s proposed visit to India has not yet been finalised, with the timing dependent on his “schedule” and the “progress” of ongoing bilateral discussions. Bangladesh foreign minister Khalilur Rahman visited India in April as part of efforts to mend strained bilateral ties.

Article Title: 'A moment that tore apart several lives': PM Modi on Partition Horrors Remembrance Day
Article Text:
Partition triggered one of the largest mass migrations in history, affecting an estimated 20 million people.

NEW DELHI: A day ahead of Independence Day , Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Friday paid tribute to those affected by the Partition of India, remembering their courage and resilience on Partition Horrors Remembrance Day.He described the day as an occasion to remember those whose lives were upended by Partition, which "tore apart several lives, uprooted families and caused immense suffering."“Today we mark Partition Horrors Remembrance Day. We recall the courage of all those who were impacted by Partition. It was a moment in history that tore apart several lives... families were uprooted, loved ones were lost, and immense suffering was endured,” PM Modi wrote in a post on X.The prime minister said that despite the hardships, those affected rebuilt their lives from scratch, overcame adversity and made significant contributions to the country's progress.“Their life journeys remind us of the strength of the human spirit. May this day deepen our resolve to preserve harmony and brotherhood in our nation and collectively work towards building a Viksit Bharat,” he added.India has observed Partition Horrors Remembrance Day on August 14 since 2021 to honour those who lost their lives or were displaced during the Partition of 1947.India gained independence from British rule on August 15, 1947. However, the birth of two new nations - India and Pakistan - was accompanied by the violent Partition, which left deep and lasting scars on millions of people.Partition triggered one of the largest mass migrations in history, affecting an estimated 20 million people. Millions were forced to leave their ancestral homes, villages, towns and cities and begin new lives as refugees.The upheaval was accompanied by widespread communal violence and the loss of countless lives, leaving a lasting impact on generations that followed.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi pays tribute to those affected by the Partition of India. Partition triggered one of the largest mass migrations in history, affecting an estimated 20 million people. India has observed Partition Horrors Remembrance Day on August 14 since 2021.

Article Title: Gen Z led student protest taught MPs how to use humour in serious political communication: Derek O' Brien

NEW DELHI: Hailing opposition unity evident in the way the INDIA bloc parties cornered the BJP led NDA in the monsoon session of Parliament, TMC’s Rajya Sabha MP Derek O’ Brien said that while the session that ended on Thursday belonged to the opposition, it was the protests over the NEET paper leaks at Jantar Mantar by youth that set the pitch for what followed in Parliament.“This was a session that belonged to the opposition. This was a win for the students and youth of the country. What they did till July 20, we the MPs had to just carry that forward. It was their win,” O’Brien said.“They taught us MPs how to use humour in serious political communication. What happened was because of the youth-student movement. Just from criticising the govt it went to ridiculing the govt,” he added citing examples of slogans coined by Gen Z to attack the govt during the protests. The TMC leader further said that a key takeaway from this session was that the opposition worked in a coordinated way.On Thursday all opposition parties had a casual meeting in the lobby of Rajya Sabha just to tell each other that all had worked as a team, an opposition MP said. He added that it was basically an assessment that the opposition really did well in the way it went about raising issues and there was a lot of unity.Opposition members highlighted that not just the INDIA bloc members but the opposition also found the way to create room for AAP which is no longer part of the grouping to speak and also DMK to make their point amid the protests in the House. The DMK distanced itself from the wider opposition INDIA bloc following friction with Congress since the latter severed its longstanding alliance with it and decided to support the TVK govt in Tamil Nadu.Going forward, the INDIA bloc parties have decided to keep up the momentum and build on the unity seen in the current session to counter the ruling dispensation till the winter session. There was also consensus that if the INDIA bloc is meeting anytime soon then the date should be announced in August itself. The bloc had held its last meeting on June 8 and had announced that they propose to meet next in Hyderabad in August. However, the date of the meeting is yet to be decided.
Article Summary: TMC’s Rajya Sabha MP Derek O’ Brien said that while the session that ended on Thursday belonged to the opposition, it was the protests over the NEET paper leaks at Jantar Mantar by youth that set the pitch for what followed in Parliament. NEW DELHI: The Trinamool Congress is preparing to move the Supreme Court against the 20 rebel Lok Sabha MPs who merged with the Nationalist Citizens Party of India. A disqualification petition will be filed within 10 days, TMC sources said.TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee had met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Wednesday to reiterate his demand for a speedy decision on the disqualification petitions submitted by TMC in June. Later addressing the media, Banerjee had expressed concern over the lack of any action on the matter so far and said that he did not receive any satisfactory response.“If the Speaker does not decide on these petitions within the period required by law and applicable judicial directions, I will be compelled to approach the Supreme Court and seek its intervention,” Banerjee said.Banerjee had earlier met Birla on July 27 in Parliament urging him to expedite his decision on pending petitions seeking disqualification of the 20 MPs, elected on TMC symbol, who have aligned with NCPI.Banerjee, a Lok Sabha MP, had also sought revocation of changes made to the seating arrangements of his party’s MPs to allow the rebel members to sit separately. He had submitted separate letters to the speaker on each of his concerns.In one of the two letters, Banerjee stated, “More than five weeks have elapsed since filing of the petitions. To date, no notices have been issued, no hearings have been scheduled, and no procedural directions appear to have been passed. Such continued action is a matter of grave concern.” On June 19, a TMC delegation led by Banerjee had submitted the 20 disqualification petitions to Birla.He had said the urgency of the matter has been further accentuated by the decision of parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju to invite the members against whom the disqualification petitions are pending, as a separate group, to the all-party meeting held on July 19. “Such developments underscore the imperative for an expeditious determination of the petitions,” he stated to emphasise his point.
Article Summary: The Trinamool Congress is preparing to move the Supreme Court against the 20 rebel Lok Sabha MPs. A disqualification petition will be filed within 10 days, TMC sources said. TMC national general secretary Abhishek Banerjee had met Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla on Wednesday.

Article Title: From New York to Delaware: US states to commemorate 'India Day' on August 15
Article Text:
US states proclaim August 15 as 'India Day' (representative image)

Delaware honours Indian-American community

New York, New Jersey also recognise August 15

How US communities celebrate India's Independence Day

India marks 80th Independence Day with focus on youth

Delaware has proclaimed August 15, 2026, as ‘India Day’, joining New York and New Jersey in recognising India's Independence Day and the contributions of the Indian-American community ahead of the country's 80th Independence Day.The proclamation was issued by Delaware Governor Matthew Meyer, who highlighted the state's growing Indian-American community and its contributions to the state's social and economic life.The development was shared by the Consulate General of India in New York on August 13.According to the proclamation, Delaware is strengthened by the many cultures and traditions represented across its communities, including its Indian-American population.The proclamation said Delawareans of Indian heritage have enriched the state through their work, leadership and service, contributing to shared prosperity and creating opportunities for future generations.It also highlighted India's diversity of languages, traditions, faiths and customs, noting that generations of Indian Americans have carried these traditions forward while building communities in the US.The proclamation said India Day would provide an opportunity to honour India's independence, celebrate the heritage and achievements of Delaware's Indian-American community and recognise the enduring connections between Delaware and the people of India.Governor Meyer encouraged residents to participate in the observance and recognise the contributions of the state's Indian-American community.Delaware's proclamation follows similar declarations by New York and New Jersey, which recognised August 15, as India's Independence Day.New Jersey governor Mikie Sherrill issued a proclamation recognising Indian Independence Day across the state. According to the Consulate General of India in New York, the proclamation highlighted the Indian-American community's contributions to New Jersey in areas including education, healthcare, research, technology, business, public service and community leadership.New York Governor Kathy Hochul also proclaimed August 15 as India Independence Day across the state.The Consulate said New York's proclamation recognised the Indian-American community's contribution to the state's cultural, economic and civic life, while also highlighting the enduring ties between India and the US.The Consulate thanked Hochul for the recognition, saying the proclamation celebrated India's journey of independence and the democratic values shared by the two countries.India's Independence Day is marked across the US each year through flag-hoisting ceremonies, parades, cultural programmes and community events.Indian diplomatic missions, including the Embassy of India in Washington and Indian consulates, hold special programmes on August 15. The Indian mission to the United Nations also participates in commemorative events.Indian-American communities across states organise cultural performances and public celebrations, with local political leaders often participating and highlighting the community's contributions to American society.Prominent landmarks have also joined the celebrations in previous years, including the Empire State Building in New York and the Space Needle in Seattle, which have been illuminated in the colours of the Indian tricolour for Independence Day events.The proclamations come as India prepares to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026.This year's celebrations will also focus on the commemoration of 150 years of ‘Vande Mataram’, while placing particular emphasis on ‘Yuva Shakti’ or youth power.The celebrations are expected to combine the historical significance of India's freedom movement with recognition of the achievements and contributions of its younger generation.The growing number of US states formally recognising India's Independence Day also underlines the visibility of the Indian-American community and the broader social, economic and cultural ties between India and the United States.
Article Summary: Delaware joins New York and New Jersey in recognising India's Independence Day. Proclamation was issued by Governor Matthew Meyer, who highlighted the state's growing Indian-American community. New York Governor Kathy Hochul also proclaimed August 15 as India Independence Day across the state. The proclamations come as India prepares to celebrate its 80th Independence Day on August 15, 2026.

Article Title: SAD chief Sukhbir Badal attacked: 62-year-old assailant had been working at Nanded gurdwara for 2 years as 'sevadar'
Article Text:
The SAD chief was visiting the gurdwara with his wife. (File photo)

NEW DELHI: Shiromani Akali Dal (SAD) chief and former Punjab deputy chief minister Sukhbir Singh Badal was injured after being attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra's Nanded on Thursday. The assailant, identified as 62-year-old Jaspal Singh , had been working at the same gurdwara for the past two years as a 'sevadar' (volunteer/attendant).According to police, the attack took place when Badal was visiting Mata Sahib Gurdwara in the Hazur Sahib area. The attacker allegedly tried to stab the Akali Dal leader in the stomach, news agency IANS reported quoting sources."... Near the stairs, a 'sevadar' (volunteer/attendant) suddenly approached and attempted to attack with his 'kirpan'... Immediately following the incident, we took the attacker into custody, and interrogation is currently underway. He is approximately 60–62 years old and has been working as a 'sevadar' at the Gurudwara for about two years," Nanded Police SP Nilabh Rohan said."Initially, he himself stated that he was angry about the drug issue in Punjab... No connection to any gang has been established ... The exact reason is not yet clear. We are currently interrogating him ... The Nanded Police and the ATS are collaborating on the case," he added.Security personnel accompanying Badal intervened immediately and overpowered the attacker before he could inflict more serious injuries.Police later identified the accused as Jaspal Singh, son of Teja Singh and a resident of Solapur Bazaar in Pune. Investigators said he had been residing at Mata Sahib Gurdwara for the last two years.Badal sustained an injury to his hand and was rushed to Yasho Sai Hospital in Nanded for treatment. Officials said that he received stitches on his hand and is in stable condition.Inspector Santosh Kendre of the Maharashtra Police's Special Protection Unit (SPU), who was deployed for Badal's security, was also injured while trying to stop the attacker.The SPU is a specialised unit tasked with providing security to VVIPs during their visits and movements.Badal was accompanied by his wife, SAD MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal, during his visit to Takht Sri Hazur Sahib. Punjab security personnel and Maharashtra Police officers were also present when the attack took place.Maharashtra CM Devendra Fadnavis has sought a detailed report from the Nanded Superintendent of Police and ordered an inquiry into the motive behind the attack. He also spoke to Badal over the phone to inquire about his condition.Police have detained the accused and launched an investigation into the circumstances that led to the attack. Security has been tightened in and around the gurdwara premises.This was not the first attack on the Akali Dal leader.In December 2024, Badal survived an assassination attempt outside the Golden Temple in Amritsar while performing 'sewadar' duties after the Akal Takht had pronounced religious punishment on him and several other party leaders over decisions taken during the SAD government's tenure between 2007 and 2017.
Article Summary: Sukhbir Singh Badal injured after being attacked at a gurdwara in Maharashtra's Nanded. The assailant, identified as 62-year-old Jaspal Singh, had been working at the same gurwara for the past two years as a'sevadar' (volunteer/attendant) Badal sustained an injury to his hand and was rushed to Yasho Sai Hospital.

NEW DELHI: Air India group has from Thursday started 'mandatory substance screening' for all pilots following the Phuket-Delhi flight serious incident. The move comes to “protect and sustain” the trust AI had earned over the decades that has been shaken by the pilot-in-command of the Phuket flight testing positive for marijuana. Aviation secretary Samir Sinha had in clear terms asked AI to “take responsibility” and do whatever it takes to ensure safety.AI senior VP (flight operations) captain Manish Uppal wrote to all pilots on Thursday: “For decades, Air India has been the flag bearer of Indian aviation. Over this time the professionalism, skill and commitment to safety of our pilots, together with other staff, has earned the trust of millions of passengers and the wider community. This trust is our most important asset, and it is vital that we do all possible to protect and sustain it. Many of you have recently reached out to share the same sentiment.”“As you know, Air India already fully complies with all regulatory requirements prescribed by India's DGCA, which are similar to those practiced in other major aviation jurisdictions including Europe and the US. We nevertheless now feel it is important to go further.Accordingly we have decided to undertake a full screening of all group pilots for any substances or medications that are not permitted under prevailing regulations. This testing is mandatory and will start today, 13 August 2026.”“It will be conducted concurrently with training at the Gurugram Academy, post flight at our Flight Briefing Centres / Air India Offices, or at locations provided by your respective bases. This initiative, which goes beyond regulatory requirements, reflects our determination to uphold the highest standards of safety and professionalism, and to provide reassurance to our passengers, stakeholders and the community at large. Thank you for your continued professionalism, dedication and commitment to maintaining the trust placed in Air India. Should you require any clarification, contact your Chief Pilot and/or Base Manager,” it says.
Article Summary: Air India group has from Thursday started'mandatory substance screening' for all pilots. Move comes to 'protect and sustain' the trust AI had earned over the decades. Pilot-in-command of Phuket flight tested positive for marijuana. Aviation secretary Samir Sinha had in clear terms asked AI to 'take responsibility'

The 2024 incident needs to be investigated, as does the role of the Punjab Police at that time. What was their connection to Narain Chaura? Only then will it become clear who is behind this. Article Summary: Shiromani Akali Dal president Sukhbir Singh Badal was attacked on Thursday inside Nanded gurdwara. He was taken to a hospital as he sustained injuries on his hand. Article Title: Parliament Monsoon Session concludes: Key takeaways from the final day of proceedings
Article Text:
Monsoon session of the Parliament concluded on Thursday

Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha adjourned sine die

Rijiju flags low Parliament productivity

Six stanzas of Vande Mataram played in Lok Sabha

Kharge raises ‘purification’ row in Rajya Sabha

Modi and Shah present as session closes

Bills: 12 introduced, 11 passed by both Houses

NEET protests and the political battle that dominated the session

The wider legislative and political legacy

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Parliament’s Monsoon Session concluded on Thursday with both Houses adjourned sine die after weeks marked by legislative business, opposition protests and repeated disruptions over the Jantar Mantar protest and other political flashpoints.The Lok Sabha’s final morning was strikingly brief. In just three minutes and 10 seconds, members assembled, all six stanzas of Vande Mataram were rendered, MPs including Prime Minister stood to attention, and Speaker Om Birla adjourned the House sine die.The closing proceedings unfolded amid familiar slogans, with the Opposition shouting “apologise, apologise” and “who ordered the lathi-charge?” as home minister Amit Shah entered. Birla also skipped his customary valedictory remarks on the House’s performance, underscoring a session dominated by disruption. Rajya Sabha witnessed Mallikarjun Kharge remarks over Haldwani 'Suddhikaran' row followed by JP Nadda's clarification and condemnation of the event.Meanwhile, in Rajya Sabha, leader of opposition Mallikarjun Kharge raised the Haldwani ‘suddhikaran’ row, alleging that a havan was conducted at the venue after his rally. Leader of the House JP Nadda condemned the incident and assured Kharge that the matter would be investigated.The Lok Sabha was adjourned sine die by Speaker Om Birla at 11.06 am, followed by the Rajya Sabha, bringing the 19-sitting Monsoon Session to an end. The session had been scheduled from July 20 to August 13. Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju had said before the session that the government wanted the Houses to see “meaningful debate, discussion and decisions on issues of National importance”.The closing proceedings, however, came amid a continuing logjam over the opposition’s demand for a government response to the police action against students protesting the NEET controversy.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said 12 Bills were passed during the Monsoon Session, but acknowledged that parliamentary discussion remained limited. “It was a good session…we have passed 13 bills; but it was not a good session in terms of discussion,” he said. Lok Sabha productivity stood at 19%, compared with 39% in Rajya Sabha, he added. He also accused the Opposition of avoiding debate despite the government’s willingness to discuss issues.On the last day of the Monsoon Session, Lok Sabha proceedings opened with all six stanzas of Vande Mataram on Thursday, marking a first for Parliament. Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and other senior leaders were present. The move followed fresh Union home ministry directions on the National Song’s protocol. During the session, Parliament also passed the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Bill, providing statutory protection around national symbols.Congress president and leader of opposition in the Rajya Sabha Mallikarjun Kharge used the final day to raise an alleged “purification” ritual at the Ramlila Maidan in Haldwani after his public meeting there.Kharge said, “I was in Haldwani where I made a public speech at Ramlila Maidan. Lakhs of people were there. At that time, I did not mention the name of any community or religion; I only reiterated the issues of the Govt. But after my speech, people of BJP performed a ‘havan’ there to ‘purify’ that stage...Is this the way in a democracy? How are you protecting the Constitution? I am the LoP.”Union minister JP Nadda responded that the BJP did not support such an act and said it would be investigated. “BJP does not subscribe to such activities. Never. But we will investigate this. I assure you that whatever happened there will certainly be investigated,” Nadda said, adding that he condemned the incident.PM Narendra Modi and Union HM Amit Shah were present during the closing proceedings, as the student protest controversy remained the dominant unresolved political issue. The Opposition had demanded Shah’s statement and his presence in the Houses over the police action during the July 20 march by students towards Parliament.On Wednesday, Shah said the government was prepared for a detailed discussion. “As far as the discussion is concerned, Kiren Rijiju, who is our parliamentary affairs minister, has made it very clear that the government is ready to discuss every aspect of the student protests regarding NEET,” Shah said.He added, “On my part, I have also said that I am ready to answer any question in Parliament. But they don't want the discussion to happen at all. Now let the public decide who is running away.”Rahul Gandhi rejected the offer, saying the Opposition was not interested in an “Amit Shah lecture” and questioning who ordered the use of force against protesting students.The Monsoon Session saw 12 Bills introduced, with 10 cleared by both Houses, according to PRS Legislative Research. Key legislation covered public examinations, national honour, birth and death registration, the Supreme Court, MSMEs, taxation, tribunals, cooperative development, Kerala’s name and mining.The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill received the most debate, 17 hours and 34 minutes across both Houses. Several other Bills passed with limited discussion, including four minutes each for the birth and death registration and Supreme Court judges Bills.The NEET controversy and police action against student protesters dominated the Monsoon Session, with the Opposition demanding a debate on alleged examination irregularities, education minister Dharmendra Pradhan’s resignation and accountability for the July 20 crackdown. Repeated protests led to adjournments, while the government said it was ready for discussion.The Opposition, however, linked any debate to accountability over the alleged police action. The issue remained unresolved at the session’s close. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi asked, “Who shot the students? Who gave the order to beat up the students with lathis with nails?”Beyond the NEET confrontation, the session produced a broad legislative package. Parliament cleared the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Bill, raising the sanctioned strength of Supreme Court judges other than the Chief Justice from 33 to 37; the MSME Development Amendment Bill; taxation amendments; the Tribunals Reforms Bill; the Kerala (Alteration of Name) Bill; the National Cooperative Development Corporation Amendment Bill and the Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill.The Kerala Bill was among the final measures passed, clearing the Lok Sabha on August 11 and the Rajya Sabha on August 12. The Mines and Minerals Amendment Bill cleared the Rajya Sabha on the final day.The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill became another major political flashpoint. Instead of being passed, it was referred to a Joint Parliamentary Committee for detailed scrutiny amid Opposition demands that it be withdrawn.
Article Summary: Lok Sabha, Rajya Sabha adjourned sine die after weeks marked by legislative business, opposition protests and disruptions. Speaker Om Birla skipped his customary valedictory remarks on the House’s performance. Opposition shouting “apologise, apologise” and “who ordered the lathi-charge?” as home minister Amit Shah entered.

Article Title: Use medical tourists' money to treat poor Indians: Panel
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Revenue earned from foreign patients and affluent Indians should help fund treatment for poorer patients, a Parliamentary Standing Committee on Health and Family Welfare has recommended, proposing that corporate hospitals adopt a cross-subsidisation model to make advanced healthcare more affordable.The panel said hospitals that benefit from government concessions such as subsidised land, tax incentives and 100% foreign direct investment (FDI) should earmark part of the revenue generated from medical tourism and high-paying patients to provide advanced tertiary care to economically weaker Indians.The recommendation is part of the committee's report on the affordability and accessibility of healthcare, which noted that India's corporate hospital sector has recorded strong growth driven by high-value procedures, rising medical tourism and increasing revenue per occupied bed. While acknowledging India's emergence as a global healthcare destination, the panel said the benefits of this growth must also reach patients who cannot afford expensive treatment.Observing that private health insurance penetration in India remains low and out-of-pocket expenditure continues to push many families into financial distress, the committee said a structured cross-subsidy mechanism could improve access to life-saving tertiary care for poorer patients.It said hospitals receiving government support should share part of the gains from medical tourism and premium-paying patients with economically weaker sections.The panel also recommended that corporate hospitals reserve a defined quota of beds under government-funded health insurance schemes such as Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY at standard package rates to ensure that beneficiaries have access to advanced treatment at leading private hospitals.To address the uneven distribution of healthcare infrastructure, the committee proposed linking government incentives, including subsidised land, tax benefits and FDI facilitation, to investment in tier-2, tier-3 and rural areas. It also recommended expanding public-private partnerships and extending financial and technology support to smaller hospitals in underserved regions.The recommendations form part of a broader roadmap to make healthcare more affordable. The committee has also proposed capping private hospital room rents in major metropolitan cities at the average tariff of nearby three-star hotels, standardising treatment package rates, improving price transparency and expanding government health spending to reduce out-of-pocket expenditure.
Article Summary: Hospitals receiving government support should share part of the gains from medical tourism and premium-paying patients with economically weaker sections. The panel also recommended that corporate hospitals reserve a defined quota of beds under government-funded health insurance schemes such as Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY.

NEW DELHI: Punjab Governor Gulab Chand Kataria on Thursday said he has recommended parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara, who is serving a life sentence for the assassination of former chief minister Beant Singh and had sought relief to meet his ailing mother.His statement came a day after Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Mann urged Kataria to intervene and facilitate Hawara’s parole.Former Union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu, who is the former chief minister's grandson, had also called for Hawara to be granted parole. Beant Singh was killed in a suicide bombing in Chandigarh in 1995."His mother is unwell. We have recommended his case on humanitarian grounds,” Kataria told reporters.The governor’s intervention was required as Hawara’s parole plea is being considered in Delhi.Earlier, Mann on Wednesday backed parole for Hawara on humanitarian grounds, saying his ailing mother had a “renewed hope” of meeting her son after 31 years.The chief minister said Kataria, who is also the administrator of Chandigarh, had assured him that he would take up the matter with the Union home secretary. Mann had earlier written to Kataria, seeking 10-day parole for Hawara.Bittu, meanwhile, expressed hope that the competent authorities would consider the request expeditiously and take an appropriate decision in accordance with law.He reiterated that while his family would always honour the “supreme sacrifice” of Beant Singh, it also believed that compassion, humanity and peace should guide society forward.Last month, the Punjab and Haryana high court directed authorities at Delhi’s Mandoli prison, where Hawara is lodged, to decide his parole application in a time-bound manner after obtaining recommendations from the Chandigarh administration.Kataria, the Punjab governor, also serves as the administrator of Chandigarh.Hawara was initially sentenced to death, but the sentence was later commuted by the high court. Article Title: Phuket plunge: Airbus sends initial report to AI, seeks maintenance details
Article Text:
Airbus has asked Air In- dia to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activi- ties as it continues its event assessment

NEW DELHI: “The elevators (control up and down movement of aircraft) and ailerons (controls left and right movement) surfaces were lost for around four seconds.” Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.“Based on analysis of the DFDR (digital flight data recorder),” Airbus found that within seven seconds between 9:32:44 am and 9:32:51 am, there was a loss of hydraulics systems — pressurised fluids which enable flight controls to move. At this point, the autopilot was disconnected and the aircraft’s nose went up (increase in pitch). All timings are in IST.The Airbus preliminary communication sent to AI on Aug 10 says “at (9:32:46 am) auto pilot 2 was disconnected, and full nose down (pitch down) input began being applied on first officer side with no direct response from the flight control surfaces” due to the loss of hydraulics. Five seconds later, a single hydraulic system was recovered and a few seconds later the remaining two systems were back, leading to recovery of normal flight control.Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities as it continues its event assessment. “Since load exceedances were detected during the sudden altitude change, (maintenance) inspections must be performed.Please provide the inspection results once they are completed. Please provide more detailed pilot reports from the reported event clarifying what it is observed during the event,” the communication says.“...this event requires an analysis considering both aircraft systems and structural integrity, as airframe may have been affected by the movement,” it adds.While probe is on by Airbus and France’s accident investigator under the ambit of India’s Aircraft Accident Investigation Bureau, several pilots are questioning why Air India decided to fly the aircraft all the way to Delhi after it had recovered from the technical events.
Article Summary: Airbus has asked Air India to carry out multiple tests and share the aircraft’s recent maintenance activities. Airbus, in its initial assessment of the A320 flying from Phuket to Delhi on Aug 4, said the aircraft experienced a sudden loss in altitude that left 24 injured.

Article Title: BCI bars Nalsar students over CJI Surya Kant protest, retracts

NEW DELHI: If the directive was unusual, the withdrawal was dramatic.Bar Council of India (BCI) on Thursday took back its communication — hours after issuing it — to Hyderabad-based Nalsar University of Law that said those who organised opposition to the invitation to CJI Surya Kant for the institute’s convocation would not be enrolled as advocates.In a fresh communication late evening, BCI chairperson Manan Kumar Mishra said the council had “thoroughly discussed and deliberated” on his earlier letter to Nalsar’s vice-chancellor and state bar council secretaries and modified its direction.BCI — the statutory regulating body for legal education and profession — is of the unanimous view that, according to the “latest report”, vast majority of Nalsar’s 2026 graduating students were innocent and “were not inclined to take part in the move of disrespect”, he said. However, Mishra said, “It has been further reported by some reliable sources that a handful of teachers and outsiders were instrumental in instigating innocent students. ” BCI will wait for the “inquiry report” from Nalsar, he said in the fresh letter, which he posted on his X handle.SCBA president Vikas Singh reacted sharply to BCI chairperson’s earlier letter to Nalsar by condemning its ‘arbitrary’ decision to stall enrolment of law graduates from the university.Singh said the decision is illegal, disproportionate and fundamentally unsustainable. However, he said he did not support the section of students who opposed the invitation to the CJI.This story continues on page 10 in the newspaper. For your reading convenience we have added it below.Disrespectful law students are a liability, says BCI chiefIn his earlier letter to one of India’s top law schools, Mishra had sought a “factual report” about the persons instrumental in “intimidation of a constitutional functionary” by initiating, organising or mobilising the campaign against participation of CJI at the convocation ceremony.BCI chairperson had said, “Till further orders, no student of Nalsar University of Law, who has obtained law degree in the year 2026, shall be enrolled by any state bar council as an advocate.” He said a final decision on this issue would be taken on Aug 19 after receiving a report from VC.The council had requested Nalsar to differentiate between persons who have merely signed or supported the representations from those who organised or coordinated the campaign and those who proposed or mobilised an actual boycott, obstruction or disruption. “BCI does not, at this stage, record that any person stands disqualified from enrolment under Section 24A (of Advocates Act) merely on account of participation in the aforesaid representation or campaign,” Mishra had said in his first letter.TOI on Aug 10 had reported that a section of students at Nalsar had requested the university to reconsider inviting CJI Kant for its upcoming convocation taking exception to CJI’s remarks during the hearing on alleged police excesses against student protesters’ march to Parliament on July 20. The petitioner wanted the CJI-led bench to go through the video footage of police action. CJI turned down the plea saying he did not have time to watch videos.The university has not yet finalised the date of convocation, for which the CJI had been traditionally invited as the chief guest.In his first communication, the BCI chief had said, “A student of Law, having no regard or respect for the highest judicial office of the country, is not expected to be a responsible or sensible advocate, teacher or a judge. Such persons shall always be a liability on the profession. Such conduct reflects adversely upon the person’s suitability for entry into or association with the legal profession and is inconsistent with the dignity, discipline and ethical standards of the legal profession.” He said, “As per some reliable sources, there exists groupism and dirty politics among some of the academic staff and they have played a very active role in misleading, instigating and misguiding the students. This is a very serious matter. The teachers, instead of involving themselves in their teaching job, are doing nasty politics in the campus. BCI, being the regulator of Legal Education cannot be a mute spectator of such a serious situation.”“However, where material concerning the conduct of a particular applicant is under active statutory examination by the BCI and such examination may have a bearing upon regulatory considerations governing entry into the profession, completion of enrolment during pendency of such examination may create a fait accompli and render the statutory examination ineffective,” it had said asking the state bar councils to withhold registration of law graduates from Nalsar till further orders.
Article Summary: Bar Council of India (BCI) on Thursday took back its communication to Hyderabad- based Nalsar University of Law that said those who organised opposition would not be enrolled as advocates. The decision follows a campaign by the students againsts the participation of CJI Surya Kant in the convocation ceremony.

Article Title: Indian officials likely to join Taliban’s Victory Day celebrations
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: As India and the Taliban-ruled Afghanistan further intensify their pragmatic engagement focused on trade, humanitarian aid, and regional security, the Taliban will celebrate the fifth anniversary of the Victory Day in the Afghanistan embassy here on Monday, next week. Victory Day is observed annually by the Taliban on August 15 to commemorate the group's return to Kabul in 2021, following the withdrawal of US-led NATO forces.The invitation for the event has been extended by Afghanistan charge d’affaires Mufti Noor Ahmad Noor and carries the emblem of the Islamic Emirate of Afghanistan. According to sources, who spoke on condition of anonymity, the event is not just endorsed by the Indian side but is will also see participation by senior Indian officials.India doesn’t officially recognise the Islamic Emirate, maintaining its position on that issue is in consonance with the international community, although it has allowed the Taliban to take control of the Afghan embassy. However, its position is also marked by pragmatic engagement with Taliban, leveraging its historic goodwill and development presence to protect its security and regional interests. These efforts have been further aided by the dramatic shift in the Taliban’s ties with Pakistan.India and Afghanistan continue to back each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity with India solidly standing by Kabul in the latter’s border conflict with Pakistan. Much to Pakistan’s chagrin, the Taliban too backed India’s sovereignty over J&K in a joint statement with India last year by endorsing a mention of the union territory as located in India, while condemning the Pahalgam terrorist attack.While restoring its own embassy in Kabul last year, India had agreed to the appointment of Taliban diplomats here, allowing them to work out of the embassy even in the absence of a formal recognition for the Taliban regime. The development followed a landmark visit by Afghanistan foreign minister Amir Khan Muttaqi to India that further cemented the relationship.India’s historical and civilizational ties with Afghanistan, along with the development partnership, has witnessed more than 500 projects spread across each of the 34 provinces of the country in critical areas of power, water supply, road connectivity, healthcare, education, agriculture and capacity building.
Article Summary: The Taliban will celebrate the fifth anniversary of the Victory Day in the Afghanistan embassy here on Monday, next week. NEW DELHI: Parliament Thu-rsday passed Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which seeks to restrict states’ powers to levy taxes on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands. Govt said the new law doesn’t seek to interfere with the autonomy of states, but aims to ensure uniform mineral rates.Lok Sabha passed the bill Wednesday, while Rajya Sabha cleared it Thursday. While no Congress MP participated in the discussion, others in the opposition, including DMK, BJD, RJD and Left parties, raised questions on whether the law would adversely impact revenues of state govts.Replying to the debate, mines minister G Kishan Reddy said Centre was seeking to regulate major minerals such as coal, limestone, iron ore, copper and manganese, while states would continue to have powers over 49 minor minerals.Reddy alleged coal blocks allocated during UPA’s tenure were a “scam” while claiming mineral allocations over the past 12 years had been transparent. He said states’ share of mineral revenue had risen from 65% in 2014-15 to 85% now, while their share of coal revenue had increased from 51% to 96%. He said Centre receives only about 11% of mineral revenue, with 88% going to states, and asserted that no state would suffer any revenue loss.Jharkhand CM Hemant Soren, however, announced a statewide agitation against the legislation, warning that “the entire nation will witness its scale” if Centre did not withdraw it. Kerala CM VD Satheesan also said his govt would oppose the new law, alleging the proposed changes would encroach upon powers of states over land. tnn
Article Summary: Parliament passed Mines and Minerals (Development and Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026. Law seeks to restrict states’ powers to levy taxes on mineral rights and mineral-bearing lands. Govt said the new law doesn’t seek to interfere with the autonomy of states, but aims to ensure uniform mineral rates.

Article Title: 'No clear information': Nepal ‘loses’ papers of centuries-old treaty defining borders with India
Article Text:
Nepali PM Balen Shah had raised up the issue of border with India, including Lipulekh.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

What is the Sugauli Treaty?

NEW DELHI: Nepal has apparently lost the decades-old original of the 1816 Treaty of Sugauli, a document that largely defined the Himalayan nation's boundaries with British India, its foreign minister Shisir Khanal told Parliament on Monday.Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the House of Representatives recently that while some treaty-related documents are held in the National Archives, their status as the original official documents remains unclear.“The Government of Nepal does not have clear information on whether we possess the official treaty documents. There are records showing that some documents related to certain treaties are kept at the National Archives. But we do not have clear information as to whether those are the actual official treaties,” Khanal said.He said Nepal does have documents related to the 1816 Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship with India.The disclosure comes amid renewed tensions over the Nepal-India border after India and China agreed to reopen the Lipulekh trade route. Nepal claims Lipulekh, Limpiyadhura and Kalapani as its territories, while India maintains that they are part of its territory.This becomes significant, as the dispute resurfaced recently after Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah said Kathmandu had raised with India concerns over alleged encroachment, including in Lipulekh. Shah said both sides had agreed to examine the issue through historians, surveyors and territorial experts and resolve it through diplomatic talks. He also called for the UK to be involved, citing its role in shaping the region's borders during the colonial era. Shah said Nepal had found that “not only had India encroached on Nepal's land, but Nepal had also encroached on India's land in multiple places.”India rejected any role for third parties, with MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal having said “there is no role for any third parties in a bilateral matter between India and Nepal.” He said nearly 98% of the boundary had been demarcated, with remaining issues including stretches affected by the shifting Gandak River and cross-border occupation or encroachment on no-man's land. India has also rejected Nepal's claims over Lipulekh, Kalapani and Limpiyadhura as “neither justified nor based on historical facts and evidence. ”The issue of missing treaty documents has been around for years. In 2016, when the Eminent Persons’ Group on Nepal-India Relations began discussions on reviewing or replacing the 1950 treaty, Nepal tried to locate the original but failed to find it. The government subsequently provided the Bhekh Bahadur Thapa-led committee with another copy of the treaty.The matter later prompted a parliamentary inquiry. On July 22, the Delegated Legislation and Governance Committee of Nepal's National Assembly concluded that the original copies of both the Sugauli Treaty and the 1950 Treaty of Peace and Friendship could not be found in the country.The committee said it searched various locations where historical records could have been preserved, including libraries, archives and government repositories, as well as the Department of Archaeology, Narayanhiti Palace Museum, Ministry of Law and Ministry of Foreign Affairs.The matter had also come up in Parliament in 2019. Then Foreign Minister Pradeep Gyawali said the government had copies of both treaties but was unsure whether they were originals. “We have both treaties, but we have to forensically verify whether these copies are originals or not,” Gyawali had said. “We are also trying to find historical documents and maps in India and the United Kingdom.”Khanal's remarks came as he outlined a broader plan to review Nepal's existing international agreements. He said the country has 655 treaties and agreements, including 412 bilateral and 243 multilateral agreements.Of these, 55 have already been concluded or amended, while the government plans to review the remaining 600 based on their necessity and relevance. Khanal said older or inactive agreements would be reviewed, amended or renewed in coordination with the countries or international organisations concerned.“Under the general principles of international treaty law, the review, amendment, or renewal of any bilateral or multilateral treaty or agreement depends on the mutual consent and approval of the concerned state parties or relevant international organisations,” Khanal said.He added that the government would undertake the exercise with the cooperation and approval of the relevant countries and international organisations.The Sugauli Treaty was agreed between Nepal and the British East India Company after the Anglo-Nepalese War. It was signed in December 1815 and ratified in March 1816, with the agreement establishing the basis for Nepal's territorial boundary with British India.The treaty required Nepal to cede significant territories to the East India Company and renounce claims to lands west of the Kali River, while also setting out provisions governing relations between Nepal and the Company.
Article Summary: Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal told the House of Representatives that while some treaty-related documents are held in the National Archives, their status as the original official documents remains unclear. The disclosure comes amid renewed tensions over the Nepal-India border after India and China agreed to reopen the Lipulekh trade route.

Article Title: 2027 UP assembly elections: How parties are vying for Dalit votes amid Mayawati’s shrinking base
Article Text:
As Mayawati's base shrinks, BJP, SP and Congress intensify fight for Dalit votes in UP

From 206 seats to one: How BSP lost ground

BJP's Dalit outreach gets sharper ahead of 2027

SP’s Dalit outreach

How Samajwadi Party performed when they contested independently

Congress tries to reclaim lost ground

Chandrashekhar Azad adds another claimant

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Dalit politics in Uttar Pradesh is at a crossroads. For a very long time, Mayawati and her Bahujan Samaj Party were synonymous with the idea of Dalit vote in UP. Not any more. Mayawati’s BSP today is a much weaker force. The last three elections in the state have pushed Mayawati, the four-time chief minister of UP, to the margins of state politics. This has opened up the Dalit space and triggered an interesting scramble among political parties for a slice of the Dalit pie in the 2027 assembly elections.So, we have the BJP playing the name-change game in Bhadohi and organising a 7-month campaign to honour 15th-century saint-poet Sant Ravi Das. Then we have Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav announcing 14 extra seats for the Dalits to cement his PDA (Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak) politics. Congress too is trying to win back voters it lost decades ago. Then there is Chandrashekhar Azad, who is trying to consolidate his own space in the state.As Uttar Pradesh heads towards 2027, the question is: if the BSP continues to lose ground, where does Mayawati’s old support base go and which of her rivals stands to gain the most?The BSP’s rise in UP politics was as dramatic as its fall. The party was founded by Kanshi Ram in 1984 with the idea of giving Dalits and other marginalized communities an independent voice.Mayawati, who emerged as his political successor, took the BSP to great heights in Uttar Pradesh. Under her leadership, the BSP won a majority on its own in the 2007 assembly elections, winning 206 seats with a vote share of 30.43%.Dalits, who constitute around 21% of UP’s population as per the 2021 census, have for years been the core base of Mayawati’s Bahujan Samaj Party. But that dynamic has now changed.BSP is a much weaker force today. Mayawati has failed to mobilise Dalit support for her BSP in the last two elections in the state, thereby opening up the space for other political contenders. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BSP could win just 1 seat with a vote share of 12.88%. This was a sharp decline from the 19 seats and a 22.23% vote share that Mayawati had got in 2017.The 2024 Lok Sabha elections went on to showcase that Mayawati’s dismal 2022 performance was not an aberration. The BSP supremo failed to win even one Lok Sabha seat, while her party’s vote share dipped to 9.4% from 19.43% in 2019. Clearly, the results reinforced the gradual decline in BSP’s influence among Dalits.As Mayawati gears up for the 2027 assembly challenge, she faces an uphill road. The BSP chief has not just lost support of voters, but also control over her party. So, when Mayawati issued a stern message that all the candidates for the upcoming poll will be finalised by her and not by her nephew Akash Anand, it was an indication of the internal tussle in her party.Akash Anand, who has been in and out of Mayawati’s favour in the past, launched the party’s 2027 assembly poll campaign from Sadabad in Hathras this week.Mayawati, who has often been accused of helping the BJP, has ruled out any pre-poll alliance. She has claimed that some candidates have already been finalised for the upcoming assembly elections. Mayawati has asked party cadres to start rebuilding the party and drum up OBC support ahead of the polls. The cadres have apparently been asked to remind people of the party's past governance and convince them that the real benefit and welfare of the OBC community lie with the BSP and its "iron lady government".Mayawati, however, must consider that it will be difficult for the BSP to come back to power only by holding on to its core Dalit vote alone. It will have to recreate the Dalit-OBC combination that originally carried Mayawati to power in Lucknow with a majority of her own.One interesting fallout of BSP’s decline has been the BJP’s aggressive outreach to woo the Dalits. When Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath announced the renaming of Bhadohi district as Sant Ravidas Nagar last month, he put the BJP right at the middle of the Dalit outreach battle ahead of 2027 polls.The move also revived an old political contest over name-change politics. Mayawati was the one who had renamed Bhadohi as Sant Ravidas Nagar in December 1997. Akhilesh Yadav restored the old name in 2014. Now, by bringing Sant Ravidas Nagar back, Yogi sought to make a bigger political point, accusing the SP of erasing a Dalit symbol while positioning the BJP as a party willing to restore it.Mayawati publicly welcomed the decision, a rare moment of agreement with the ruling party. She was quick, however, to remind voters that it was her government that had changed the district's name in the first place and that the decision was later reversed under Akhilesh.The party realises that Dalit votes are up for grabs and hence is going all out to woo them. The party’s 'Samrasta Sankalp Abhiyan’ appears planned to coincide with assembly elections in two key states, Uttar Pradesh and Punjab, early next year.Both these states have a sizeable population of Dalits who play an important role in many constituencies. In the 2022 assembly elections, the BJP and its ally Apna Dal (Soneylal) together bagged 63 Scheduled Caste (SC) seats compared to 20 won by the then Samajwadi Party-led opposition alliance. But the 2024 Lok Sabha polls changed the dynamics, with the SP and the Congress winning 43 of the 80 seats in the state and pushing the BJP to make an aggressive outreach. The loss of Faizabad seat to SP's Awadhesh Prasad, a Pasi leader, was particularly significant and gave Akhilesh Yadav fresh ammunition for his PDA pitch.Earlier this year, the Yogi Adityanath government approved the “Dr B R Ambedkar Murti Vikas Yojna" under which Rs 1 crore is to be allocated to each of the state's 403 assembly constituencies for the beautification and development of statues of social reformers.The BJP's efforts to woo Dalits has also been visible in its recent Cabinet expansion. Of the six new ministers inducted into the Yogi government, two were Dalits, Krishna Paswan from the Pasi community and Surendra Singh Daler from the Valmiki community. Three others were from OBC groups. Two non-Yadav OBC ministers were also given independent charge.The BJP's primary task ahead of 2027 would be to hold on to the non-Jatav Dalit support it built over the past decade and prevent a repeat of 2024.The 2024 Lok Sabha elections also showed that the Dalits in UP were ready to back other political parties who wooed them. Dalit support played a key role in the spectacular success of Akhilesh Yadav’s Samajwadi Party, which won 37 seats in 2024.Together with its alliance partner Congress, the INDIA bloc won 43 of the 80 seats in the state, pushing the BJP on the back foot. Akhilesh Yadav, who has centred his politics around PDA (Pichhde, Dalits and Aplasankhyaks), gained from his Dalit outreach in the 2024 elections. His Samajwadi Party fielded two Dalit candidates from general seats. While one of them went on to win the all-important Faizabad seat, the other lost by just 10,585 votes to the BJP in Meerut.Little wonder, in the run-up to the 2027 assembly elections, Akhilesh has already announced plans to field 14 Dalit candidates from general seats. Uttar Pradesh has 84 seats reserved for Scheduled Castes and two for Scheduled Tribes. With 14 more candidates on general seats, the total tally of reserved candidates for SP will increase to 100. This will help reinforce his message to the Dalits in line with his PDA politics. The move will also help the SP shed the narrative of being a Muslim-Yadav party. Rahul Gandhi has made it clear that Dalits would now play a 'central role' in Congress. Before Mayawati and the BSP built their massive Dalit vote bank in the 1990s, Congress was the primary choice for Uttar Pradesh's Dalits. For nearly three decades after that, Congress was almost pushed out of UP politics.Rahul Gandhi has started his road to the UP election by acknowledging that the party had failed to take the right steps for the community in the 1980s and 1990s. He even praised Kanshi Ram for bringing Dalits together and giving the community a sense of confidence.Rahul has also made the Constitution a regular part of his social justice pitch. He is often seen carrying the red book of the Constitution while warning that constitutional rights and reservation are under threat. He has repeatedly invoked BR Ambedkar in the same pitch, asserting that Congress wants to position itself as a guardian of the Constitution.The party has also put a Dalit leader in charge of Uttar Pradesh. Rajendra Pal Gautam, who heads the Congress’s Scheduled Castes Department, has been appointed UP in-charge ahead of the 2027 polls. Interestingly, Gautam had also made an unsuccessful attempt to meet Mayawati at her Lucknow residence earlier this year.Whether the party will be able to translate this outreach into votes remains to be seen.Then there is Chandrashekhar Azad, whose 2024 victory from Nagina made him a prominent figure in UP’s Dalit politics. Unlike BJP, SP or Congress, Azad is trying to build an independent space outside the BSP. His challenge now is to take that appeal beyond one constituency and build an organisation strong enough to matter across the state in 2027.That is what makes the coming assembly election in Uttar Pradesh interesting. For decades, politics in Uttar Pradesh has revolved around caste. Political parties build their electoral strategies around social coalitions, loyalty of communities and traditional vote base.Mayawati may no longer command the Dalit vote the way she once did, but that vote bank has not disappeared. It simply has more claimants. And in 2027, where those voters eventually move could make a significant difference.
Article Summary: Dalit politics in Uttar Pradesh is at a crossroads. For a very long time, Mayawati and her Bahujan Samaj Party were synonymous with the idea of Dalit vote in UP. But that dynamic has now changed. BSP is a much weaker force today.

Article Title: SC tells UPSC to defer call on Odisha DGP pick
Article Text:
Complainant alleges bias, state says claim baseless

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday asked Union Public Service Commission to defer the selection of a panel of three officers from which the Odisha govt was to choose the successor of present DGP Y B Khurania, who retires on Aug 16.Appearing for applicant Jayant Das, senior advocate P Chidambaram told a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that a certain ADGP was hurriedly promoted to DGP rank and included in the panel of names sent by Odisha govt to UPSC , which was against the DGP selection procedure laid down by SC in the two decade-old Prakash Singh judgement.When amicus curiae and senior advocate Raju Ramachandran said the matter required consideration, Odisha advocate general Pitambara Acharya said the state had followed Prakash Singh guidelines scrupulously and sent names of 11 DGP-rank police officers to UPSC for preparation of a panel of three-most suitable officers.“The complainant has seven criminal cases pending against him and is a habitual offender. He might have a certain axe to grind against some officers. There is no breach of any procedure. We will present a clear picture before court,” Acharya said.CJI Kant pointed out that none of the aggrieved officers who might have been overlooked in the choice of 11 empaneled names have complained. UPSC, through senior advocate Hrishikesh Baruah, informed the court that the selection authority was meeting on Thursday itself.But the bench said it should not finalise the panel.Baruah then said UPSC would postpone the meeting till next date of hearing. SC asked Odisha govt to file its response to the application and posted the matter for hearing on Aug 18. This means Odisha would have to either ask Khurania to continue as DGP till further orders or appoint an ad hoc DGP till the matter gets decided by SC.On Sept 22, 2006, SC laid down guidelines for selection of DGPs in states to insulate them from political influence and had given them a tenure of two years. For last two decades, it has been supervising the appointment process for DGPs and entertaining applications which point out irregularities or illegalities in that process.
Article Summary: Supreme Court asked Union Public Service Commission to defer the selection of a panel of three officers. Odisha govt was to choose successor of present DGP Y B Khurania, who retires on Aug 16. Complainant alleges bias, state says claim baseless.

Article Title: 'No NALSAR 2026 graduate will be enrolled as advocate': BCI amid CJI convocation invite row
Article Text:
The decision follows a campaign by the students againsts the participation of CJI Surya Kant in the convocation ceremony.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Bar Council of India (BCI) has directed all state bar councils to halt the enrolment of any 2026 law graduate from NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad, as an advocate until further orders. This follows an alleged organised campaign against the participation of Chief Justice Surya Kant in the university’s convocation ceremony.The directive was issued by bar council chairman Manan Kumar Mishra, who said the Council had taken note of reports and material in the public domain regarding an organised campaign at NALSAR's convocation ceremony.The bar council has also sought an authenticated factual report from the university within three days and said the matter will be considered on August 19, after the vice-chancellor submits the report.The council has asked NALSAR to identify, on the basis of verifiable material, the persons allegedly instrumental in initiating, drafting, circulating, coordinating or mobilising the campaign. It has sought details of those involved in organising meetings, communicating with the media, administering social media or organised groups used for coordination, or proposing or mobilising any call for boycott, obstruction, disruption or organised non-participation in the convocation or any programme connected with the CJI.The bar council has also sought information on whether any student body, student bar council, students’ union or other recognised student organisation was involved in initiating, approving, coordinating or circulating the campaign. The university has also been asked to specify whether any faculty member, research scholar, alumnus or outsider participated in initiating, drafting, coordinating, advising or facilitating the campaign.In addition, the council has requested copies of relevant resolutions, minutes, agendas or other official records of meetings connected with the matter, and details of whether permission was sought or granted for any protest or organised activity and whether university rules governing student conduct or official functions were invoked.At the same time, the bar council clarified that participation in the representation or campaign would not automatically result in disqualification from enrolment. It said a distinction must be maintained between those who merely signed or supported a representation and those who organised or coordinated the campaign or proposed or mobilised an actual boycott, obstruction or disruption.The bar council said that where material concerning the conduct of a particular applicant is under statutory examination, completing enrolment during the pendency of such examination could create a fait accompli and render the examination ineffective.Accordingly, it directed that where the BCI specifically communicates the name of a person for further statutory consideration, no enrolment order should be passed in respect of that person and, if an application is already pending, the final decision should remain deferred during the inquiry.State bar councils have also been instructed to ensure that any person whose name is communicated by the bar council does not circumvent the pending examination by seeking enrolment before another state bar council. The council clarified that such communication at the preliminary stage would not itself constitute a conclusive finding of misconduct or disqualification.The bar council said any final adverse decision would be taken in accordance with the Advocates Act, 1961, the applicable rules and principles of natural justice.The communication further emphasised that legal education permits critical reasoning, debate and analysis of judicial decisions, but said there is a distinction between reasoned criticism and conduct which, if established after due examination, may involve intimidation, obstruction, organised disruption or disregard of institutional responsibilities attached to the legal profession.The communication has been issued to NALSAR University of Law as well as the secretaries of all state bar councils for necessary compliance.
Article Summary: The Bar Council of India (BCI) has directed all state bar councils to halt the enrolment of any 2026 law graduate from NALSAR University of Law, Hyderabad, as an advocate. This follows an alleged organised campaign against the participation of Chief Justice Surya Kant in the university’s convocation ceremony.

Article Title: Monsoon Session washed out; INDIA bloc skips customary tea

Congress MPs Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, KC Venugopal and other opposition netas stage a protest on Parliament premises Thursday

NEW DELHI: Marred by protests by the opposition throughout its sittings, Parliament's monsoon session turned out to be all but a washout, more so in terms of debates, and the rancour was reflected in the decision of Congress and its allies to keep away from the customary get-together over tea at Lok Sabha Speaker Om Birla's chamber at the session's conclusion.PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah - both attacked by the opposition for not attending Parliament proceedings - were present in LS as Birla skipped his practice of summing up the House's performance and brought the curtains down on the session as soon as business started.BJP squarely blamed leader of the opposition in LS Rahul Gandhi as the House's productivity plunged to a low of 19% - it was 39% for Rajya Sabha - saying proceedings were sacrificed "at the altar of his arrogance, delinquency and sense of entitlement".Congress blamed govt's refusal to heed the opposition's demands, including a discussion on the theft of donations at Ram temple and Modi's statement on the issue.Govt, however, pushed through its legislative agenda in the din, as Parliament passed 12 bills. Only one of them, Public Examination (Prevention of Unfair Means) Amendment Bill, had the opposition agreeing to discussion, as it allowed it to raise the issue of the NEET-UG paper leak student protest.The Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill was sent to a joint parliamentary committee for scrutiny due to protests from the opposition and church bodies, while govt's widely speculated move to revive a Constitution amendment bill to raise LS's strength by 50% and execute a one-third quota for women from 2029 did not come to pass.Parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju said Congress kept changing the goalpost as govt had agreed to its demands . "This is not good for democracy," he said. He reached out to Rahul to attend the tea but the LoP refused.With many in NDA of the view that some opposition MPs are unhappy with the uncompromising hardline taken by their brass, BJP kept its attack focused on Rahul.BJP spokesperson Ravi Shankar Prasad said Rahul may think such "irresponsible" conduct would benefit him but Congress was bound to suffer more electoral defeats as people did not appreciate such arrogance. "Parliament is not a theatre. It will not function under your sense of entitlement and exceptionalism. This attitude of 'my way or the highway' will not work," he said.Congress claimed govt was scared like never before. Opposition unity and solidarity was on full display, RS MP Jairam Ramesh said.RS chairperson C P Radh-akrishnan expressed concern over "persistent disorder and frequent disruptions", saying loss of working hours deprived the House of meaningful discussion and debate on matters of national importance.

Article Title: SC slams Centre &FSSAI, says you can’t take court for a ride
Article Text:
SC was hearing a plea filed by NGO '3S and Our Health Society'
