NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court Thursday slammed the Centre and the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) for not implementing its direction on 'front-of-pack warning labels' on processed food packages and said their top priority should be the health of citizens and not the interest of MNCs.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the court could not be taken for a ride. The bench said its Feb order was not merely a suggestion but a direction to FSSAI which had to be complied with. It said FSSAI was bowing down to the manufacturing industry and made it clear that if the food regulator didn't do it, the court would pass an order. It granted two weeks to FSSAI to reconsider its stance.In Feb, the court directed the Centre and the FSSAI to give top priority to the health concerns of citizens and not to the interests of multinational companies and asked it to implement a 'front-of-pack warning labels' system on processed food packages to ensure clear, front-facing symbols designed to instantly identify ingredients like sugar, salt and saturated fat, besides calories.It also rejected the Centre's contention that international standards could not be applied in India and asked whether India should remain underdeveloped.SC was hearing a plea filed by NGO '3S and Our Health Society'. The regulator informed SC consultations were held with all stakeholders in March, and a majority of industry organisations were opposed to the inclusion of 'warning labels' and favoured an approach intended to enable informed consumer decisions "without creating fear among consumers".The court asked govt to respond within two weeks. "We have made ourselves abundantly clear that we are concerned with the health of citizens... We still impress upon the Union of India to seriously consider the suggestion and take appropriate action."
Article Summary: SC was hearing a plea filed by NGO '3S and Our Health Society' Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said the court could not be taken for a ride. The bench said its Feb order was not merely a suggestion but a direction to FSSAI.

Article Title: Over 11k Indian workers died in Saudi, UAE each in 2021-25, MEA informs Parliament
Article Text:
Approximately 10 million Indian nationals reside in the six GCC countries

Saudi Arabia and the UAE accounted for the vast majority of Indian worker fatalities across Gulf countries from 2021 to 2025 - over 71% of total recorded deaths. According to figures released by ministry of external affairs (MEA) in Parliament on Thursday, Saudi Arabia topped the list with 11,923 deaths, and the UAE was second with 11,489 fatalities. Kuwait reported 3,890 deaths, Oman 2,457, Qatar 1,548 and Bahrain 1,206 deaths. Most nations experienced a sharp spike in deaths in 2021, likely correlated with Covid-19 pandemic, followed by a decline in 2022.From 2022 onwards, while countries like Bahrain and Qatar registered lower death counts, Saudi Arabia and the UAE recorded upward trends through 2024-2025. Approximately 10 million Indian nationals reside in the six GCC countries, with the UAE alone accounting for 4.5 million Indians.
Article Summary: Saudi Arabia and the UAE accounted for the vast majority of Indian worker fatalities across Gulf countries from 2021 to 2025. Approximately 10 million Indian nationals reside in the six GCC countries. Most nations experienced a sharp spike in deaths in 2021, likely correlated with Covid-19 pandemic, followed by a decline in 2022.

Article Title: Rahul Gandhi appears like a failed comedian: BJP

Several BJP functionaries came out strongly against Rahul and accused him of insulting voters

NEW DELHI: BJP slammed Rahul Gandhi on Thursday for using "vulgar and crude" language in targeting Prime Minister Narendra Modi , saying he appears less like the leader of the opposition and more like a failed stand-up comedian. Several BJP functionaries came out strongly against Rahul and accused him of insulting voters, who have elected Modi to office three times in a row."When will you grow up? Article Title: Air India begins dope test on all its 5,000 pilots
Article Text:
After this one-time mega exercise, AI will conduct dope tests according to regulatory requirement

NEW DELHI: Over 5,000 pilots of Air India and Air India Express have started undergoing "mandatory substance screening" from Thursday. The airline took this move to "protect and sustain" passenger trust - which had taken a hit after last June's Ahmedabad crash and was slowly being restored - but has been shaken yet again after the badly rattled Aug 4 Phuket-Delhi flight's pilot-in-command failed his dope test. After this one-time mega exercise, AI will conduct dope tests according to regulatory requirement, which as of now mandate at least 10% crew members be tested annually. DGCA is reviewing its rules and may go in for stricter consequences for those testing positive due to addiction issues and adopt a different approach for those who do so after taking medicines for pain, allergy and other issues. Pointing out that AI has over the decades "earned trust of millions of passengers and the wider community," AI senior VP (flight ops) Captain Manish Uppal wrote to all pilots Thursday: "...This trust is our most important asset, and it is vital that we do all possible to protect & sustain it."
Article Summary: Over 5,000 pilots of Air India and Air India Express have started undergoing "mandatory substance screening" from Thursday. The airline took this move to "protect and sustain" passenger trust. After this one-time mega exercise, AI will conduct dope tests according to regulatory requirement.

NEW DELHI: Flagging slow disposal in consumer forums, Supreme Court on Thursday said the consumer dispute redressal commissions cannot be the place for rehabilitation of retired judges and bureaucrats and said a detailed pan-India performance evaluation exercise of these quasi-judicial bodies is urgently needed.In a case relating to pay and allowances of members of consumer forums across the country of which the court had taken suo motu cognisance five years ago, a bench of CJI Surya Kant, and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said it came across a disturbing news report narrating the plight of consumers who are denied a hearing for four years. “If this is the way the consumer forums function, what benefit is it for the consumers who are mandated to approach the specialized quasi-judicial body? The members of consumer forums are asking for more and more facilities and perks. Vacancies and infrastructure in these forums remain a cause for concern. But are the forums justifying their salaries, perks and facilities? The purpose of constituting these commissions appears to have been frustrated,” the CJI said.Referring to the news item, SC said these issues have highlighted the poor disposal rate of consumer commissions including the National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC).Advocate Priyadarshi told SC that vacancy position, infrastructure and pay and allowances of members of consumer forums should be heard together. “We request the president of NCDRC to send a report with respect to — total pendency of cases, total composition of the commission (vacancies), average rate of disposal, estimated time to decide pending matters and the need for increasing the strength of the commission,” it said and sought report within two weeks.It also sought details from the states about the pendency and disposal rate of state and district commissions. JAMMU: Thirty-five years after an explosion rocked Jammu Tawi railway station, killing three people and leaving 18 others wounded, Govt Railway Police (GRP) Jammu Thursday claimed it arrested Altaf Hussain Sheikh, a fugitive terrorist wanted in the case.A native of Marhama, Bijbehara, in south Kashmir’s Anantnag district, Sheikh went underground after the April 2, 1991, attack along with two co-accused even as their accomplice, Aman Ullah Khan, was caught that day. A team verified Sheikh’s identity by examining his residential details and other particulars and found that he had established himself as a successful businessman in Bijbehara,” the spokesperson said.Sheikh was produced before the TADA court Thursday for further legal proceedings, the spokesperson added.

Article Title: CAG finds 98% shortfall in Green India Mission forest cover targets, red-flags multiple lapses
Article Text:
The Comptroller and Auditor General raised concerns about the inadequacies within the Green India Mission program, noting that the goal of increasing forest cover was far from realized over a decade. The audit pointed to significant issues in planning and financial oversight, which severely undermined the mission's objectives. Key vulnerable areas were neglected during afforestation, diminishing efforts to combat climate change.

NEW DELHI: Red-flagging lapses in the country’s ongoing programme to increase and improve green cover, the Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) has pointed out non-achievement of forest cover targets, noting that the observed increase in forest cover fell short by nearly 98% during 10 years of implementation (2015-16 to 2024-25) of the Green India Mission (GIM).Releasing the performance audit report on the Mission, CAG highlighted the wrong choice of landscape for planting trees, absence of convergence of various schemes to increase green cover, financial mismanagement, improper planning, lack of coordination and deficient monitoring behind non-achievement of the GIM’s goals.The broad objectives under the Mission were to increase forest/tree cover, improve the quality of forest/non-forest lands, improve ecosystem services, including biodiversity, hydrological services and carbon sequestration because of forest land/non-forest land, and to increase forest-based livelihood income of households living in and around forests.Underlining its key audit findings, the CAG in its report tabled in Parliament on Wednesday said, “As against the target of 1.4 million hectares (mha), improvement of forest cover quality was observed in only 0.11 mha (nearly 92% shortfall). Similarly, an increase in forest cover was observed in only 0.03 mha as against the target of 1.4 mha (nearly 98% shortfall).”It also noted that despite vulnerability being a key criterion, landscapes with low to moderate priority were selected over those more vulnerable to climate change for afforestation under the Mission.The performance audit examined the planning, implementation and monitoring of the GIM interventions in 16 states and UTs for which physical and financial targets were approved by the environment ministry during the period 2015-16 to 2024-25.Pointing out deficient monitoring, the CAG noted that 14 states even failed to provide required public web links for transparency. It flagged that audit evaluations revealed inflated data and overstated achievements, and GIS analysis showed that 70% of sampled sites had no noticeable changes attributable to GIM.
Article Summary: The Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG) has pointed out non- achievement of forest cover targets. The audit pointed to significant issues in planning and financial oversight. Key vulnerable areas were neglected during afforestation, diminishing efforts to combat climate change.

Article Title: ‘Since it’s written, it has to be done’: Law minister's delimitation push comes with Constitution jibe at Opp
Article Text:
Meghwal on delimitation and opposition

What is delimitation?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Why were Lok Sabha seats frozen?

NEW DELHI: Union law minister Arjun Ram Meghwal on Thursday said delimitation is a “constitutional mandate” and asserted that the exercise must be carried out after 2026, as provided under the Constitution.Speaking in ANI , Meghwal criticised the Opposition over its objections to delimitation, saying that while opposition leaders “carry the Constitution around with them”, they do not read its provisions.“Delimitation is a constitutional mandate. They certainly carry the Constitution around with them, but they don't actually read what is written in it,” Meghwal said.He said the Constitution provides for the freezing of Lok Sabha seats until 2026, after which delimitation must take place.“Seats are to remain frozen until 2026, after which delimitation must take place. Since it is written there, it has to be done,” the Union minister said.The concerns are particularly among southern states, that a population-based redistribution could reduce their relative representation.Delimitation is the process of redrawing the boundaries of Lok Sabha and state assembly constituencies based on population.Under Article 82 of the Constitution, the exercise is to be carried out after every census.The aim is to ensure that constituencies have broadly similar population sizes, although their geographical areas can vary significantly. Each state is allocated a certain number of seats in Parliament and its assembly based on the population figures used for delimitation.India carried out delimitation exercises in 1952, 1962 and 1972. However, the 42nd Constitutional Amendment in 1976 froze the number of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census, in part to ensure that states that had successfully implemented population-control measures were not penalised with fewer parliamentary seats.The 84th Constitutional Amendment in 2001 extended the freeze on the allocation of seats among states until after 2026.A delimitation exercise was undertaken in 2008, but it used the 1971 Census to retain the existing distribution of Lok Sabha seats among states. It primarily involved redrawing constituency boundaries.
Article Summary: Delimitation is the process of redrawing the boundaries of Lok Sabha and state assembly constituencies based on population. The aim is to ensure that constituencies have broadly similar population sizes. Each state is allocated a certain number of seats in Parliament and its assembly based on the population figures used for delimitation.
